description: After a transportation incident, the team needs to track who was notified, what facts were confirmed, which documents were filed, and what follow-up actions remain open. All schools and routes are fictional.

user_profile.persona: 40-year-old transportation operations manager responsible for incident closure
user_profile.context: The immediate response happened, but closure work often becomes diffuse once the urgent moment passes
user_profile.communication_style: Closure-focused and factual, wants notifications, facts, and open actions kept distinct

fact_sheet.fact: The incident, identified as INC-20240515-083, occurred on May 15, 2024, at 07:41 AM local time.
The incident involved Bus Route 12, which serves Northwood Elementary School.
The incident location was the northeast corner of the intersection of Maple Avenue and 4th Street.
The incident was a minor, single-vehicle collision where the bus struck a stationary street sign.
The vehicle involved was Bus #308, a 2022 Blue Bird Vision model, license plate S-BUS 8192.
Bus #308's last preventative maintenance was completed on April 28, 2024, logged under work order M-6734.
The GPS transponder ID for Bus #308 is BB-7719-A4, which confirmed the vehicle's location at the time of the incident.
The driver of Bus #308 was Arthur Finch, employee ID 88421.
Arthur Finch's last mandatory safety training certification was completed on February 10, 2024.
The on-site supervisor who responded to the scene was Maria Garcia, Lead Dispatcher.
Superintendent Helen Chao was notified by a direct phone call from Maria Garcia at 07:55 AM on May 15, 2024.
David Chen, Principal of Northwood Elementary, was notified via email and a follow-up phone call at 07:58 AM on May 15, 2024.
The 'ParentNotify' SMS alert system for all families on Route 12 was activated at 08:15 AM on May 15, 2024.
Officer Kenji Tanaka of the Maplewood Police Department (Badge #728) was notified and arrived on scene at 08:05 AM.
Brenda Miles, the district's agent at Apex Insurance, received an initial email notification at 09:30 AM on May 15, 2024.
A summary of the incident was posted to the internal #transport-incidents Slack channel by Maria Garcia at 08:10 AM.
A confirmed total of 22 students were on board Bus #308 at the time of the incident.
The on-site paramedic confirmed zero injuries among all 22 students and the driver.
A backup bus, #215, arrived at the scene at 08:22 AM to transport all students safely to school.
A preliminary mechanic's report confirmed the cause was a sudden hydraulic fluid leak in the primary brake line.
Driver Arthur Finch's written statement was filed and uploaded to the incident management system under file ID DR-20240515-88421.pdf on May 15, 2024.
The Maplewood Police Department report number is MWPD-24-008174, filed on May 15, 2024.
The post-incident vehicle inspection report is stored in the shared drive at `//fileserver/transport/inspections/2024/INC-20240515-083_Bus308.pdf`.
The official insurance claim form, Claim #APX-59382, was submitted via the Apex Insurance online portal on May 16, 2024.
OPEN: A post-incident review meeting with driver Arthur Finch is scheduled for May 22, 2024, at 10:00 AM in the main office.
OPEN: The State Department of Education Form 3B, 'School Bus Incident Report,' is due by May 30, 2024, and is currently in draft status, assigned to Maria Garcia.
OPEN: The repair of Bus #308 is pending a final brake system certification from the lead mechanic; the part is on order with an ETA of May 24, 2024.

user_needs.description: What happened in incident INC-20240515-083, when and where?
Which bus route, vehicle, and driver were involved?
user_needs.prediction_reason: Intra-group: After getting the basic incident summary, the user needs to know the specific assets and personnel involved.

user_needs.description: What are all the open follow-up actions?
Which district staff and external agencies (police, insurance) were notified?
Was the parent notification system used?
user_needs.prediction_reason: Intra-group: After reviewing official notifications, confirming the parent communication is a critical and distinct follow-up.

user_needs.description: Where can I find the driver's written statement?
user_needs.prediction_reason: CROSS-GROUP: After seeing the open action to meet with the driver (F25), the manager will want to review the driver's filed statement beforehand.

user_needs.description: What is the police report number for this incident?
user_needs.prediction_reason: CROSS-GROUP: After confirming that police were notified (F14), the next logical step for a closure-focused manager is to obtain the official report number for the file.

user_needs.description: What is the insurance claim number?
user_needs.prediction_reason: Intra-group: After getting one official report number (police), asking for the other key external number (insurance) is a natural continuation.

user_needs.description: What was the confirmed mechanical cause?
user_needs.prediction_reason: CROSS-GROUP: After identifying the specific vehicle involved, the most pressing question for an operations manager is understanding the root cause of the failure.

user_needs.description: What was the date of the vehicle's last preventative maintenance?
user_needs.prediction_reason: Intra-group: Learning of a mechanical failure immediately prompts a question about the vehicle's maintenance history to check for related issues.

user_needs.description: What is the date of the driver's last safety training certification?
user_needs.prediction_reason: CROSS-GROUP: After identifying the driver, a standard due diligence step is to verify their training and certification status. This is a valuable proactive check.

user_needs.description: Confirm the number of students on board and that there were no injuries.
Where is the post-incident vehicle inspection report located?
user_needs.prediction_reason: CROSS-GROUP: After learning the confirmed mechanical cause, the user will predictably want to see the detailed inspection report that contains the evidence.
